findings.title: Error paths: the doc says defaults are returned "when it is missing", but this bare `catch` also swallows a corrupt file (`JSON.parse` throws on a half-written config), a permission error and a directory path. Each returns `{ retries: 3, delayMs: 100 }` with no message, so a broken config silently changes behaviour. Catch the error and return defaults only for `ENOENT`; rethrow the rest. The parsed value is also returned unchecked as `{ retries, delayMs }`, so a file holding `{}` yields `undefined` for both.

Correctness: `i <= retries` makes `retries + 1` attempts, but the doc says "up to `retries` times". `withRetry(fn, 0, ...)` still calls `fn` once, `withRetry(fn, 3, ...)` calls it four times. Also the `catch` sleeps `delayMs` after the final failed attempt before throwing, delaying the error for nothing. Use `i < retries` (or document the count as retries after the first try) and skip the sleep when `i` is the last iteration.

Error paths: `writeFileSync` truncates the file and then writes, so a crash or full disk mid-write leaves a truncated config. The next `loadConfig` hits the swallowed parse error (line 7) and silently returns defaults, losing the saved values. Write to `path + '.tmp'` and `renameSync` it over `path`.
findings.reason: sandbox helper; config is written once at setup, so a torn write is not a risk here

findings.title: Duplication: `retryUpload` is line for line the same as `withRetry` (line 13 to 24), same signature, loop and sleep. Only the name and doc differ, so the off-by-one on line 15 is copied here too (line 34). Delete it and have the uploader call `withRetry`, or export `retryUpload` as an alias if the name is wanted.
loadConfig silently replaces a wrongly typed retries/delayMs with the default
